Those are warning signs, though the curve isn't clearly factory-dumped (no airdrop dump, top-3 share 6.5%, bundle share 22%, which is moderate).

Pool depth of 85.8 SOL is thin. A $20 ticket is about 0.1 SOL, so impact is manageable, but exit slippage on a 22% drawdown with a pool this size could be worse than the 1.4-5.1% round trip estimate.

If the desk buys: $5 ticket, 25% stop, 30-minute max hold. Small size reflects the thin pool and the drawdown momentum.

Refuse any size if: the coin's first-two-minute sell pressure is confirmed to be bot-driven rather than organic, the pool drops below roughly 60 SOL, or the price breaks the 22% drawdown level further before entry. My default recommendation is to skip this one; the base rates on post-graduation buys are negative and the signals here are mixed.
memos.scout:
The case for buying is thin but not zero. The brief shows 474 buyers in the last 15 minutes and $44k of volume, with net flow still positive at +14 SOL, and the coin is classed ORGANIC with no airdrop dump seen. Top-3 holder share (6.5%) and top-5 early buyer share (12%) suggest no single operator controls supply, and the bundle share (22%) is not extreme. The coin is roughly 30 minutes old and up 1.4% over that window, so it has not collapsed.

Against that, the last 15 minutes show sell SOL (174) nearly matching buy SOL (189), sell-to-buy ratio above 1 in the early post-graduation window, and a 22% drawdown from the 30-minute high. The pool is thin at 86 SOL, so our $20 ticket would carry the upper end of the fee and impact range. The name is generic. Nothing here shows demand accelerating; it shows churn around a flat price after a dip, which is the pattern most coins fail to recover from.

Verdict: no strong affirmative case. Pass unless the desk has a specific reason to take the base-rate-negative bet.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a slow fade after the 27% last-15-minute pump, with fees eating what's left. Net flow over that window is only +14.1 SOL on 188.6 SOL bought, so sellers (379) nearly match buyers (474) and sell-to-buy in the first two minutes is 1.22, meaning early sellers outweighed buyers. The 22% drawdown from the 30-minute high shows the pump is already fading. The 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost is large against a thin 85.8 SOL pool, and a $20 ticket will face more impact on exit. Bundle share of 22% and a launch bot point to some coordinated early activity, and the 23% completer share suggests graduation buyers may be rotating out. Top3 holding at 6.5% argues against a single-whale dump, but it doesn't rule out a fade. Skip.
